swarm.docs_reader: bee is a Rust library/CLI and harness for capability-scoped AI coding-agent execution. The intended production boundary is Linux eBPF LSM enforcement over per-scope cgroups, with file-open, exec, and IP egress hooks. The default harness build is host-only hardening and credential stripping, not kernel confinement. The workspace also handles external model APIs, local/remote MCP, transcripts/audit, in-process Rhai rendering, and current uncommitted SKILL.md discovery/grant work. Documented principles are deny-by-default/fail-closed, attenuation, kernel authority, and policy-as-data. Important caveats: unmatched reads are allowed, hard-link/bind-mount aliases can evade name rules, observe mode does not block, remote MCP is host-side domain-gated, and unsupported capabilities are rejected by EnforcementPlan. No SECURITY.md, changelog, CONTEXT.md, or ADRs exist. Git history is short and earlier history was reportedly lost.

surface_mapper.entry_point: Policy compile, attenuation, and enforcement planning
surface_mapper.description: Author intent is normalized/resolved, child policies checked against parents, then encoded into fixed-capacity eBPF map values.

surfaces.description: Requires active BPF LSM, BTF, cgroup v2, and elevated BPF/MAC/admin capabilities.

surfaces.entry_point: GitHub Actions and Rust dependency supply chain
surfaces.description: CI checks host crates; enforcement artifact uses an out-of-band pinned nightly/BPF build path.
Local/remote scripts use sudo, provision secrets/test files, and exercise kernel enforcement.
surfaces.trust_boundary: developer/CI shell and remote host -> root/kernel/test secrets

threats.threat: A default or unsupported build is mistaken for enforced sandboxing, so hostile tools run with host user authority.
Partial scope/map installation or stale cgroup-keyed entries create inconsistent enforcement or affect a reused cgroup id.
Compromised dependencies/toolchain or CI artifacts subvert the privileged loader or BPF program.
